narrative: Spend rose 8.2% to ₹9,917 (from ₹9,162) on 241 leads, up 28.9% from 187 — cost per lead dropped to ₹41.15, matching yesterday's read (₹41.18) and holding as the best CPL level in weeks. CTR (1.06%) and CPM (₹60.20) are essentially flat against yesterday's ₹59.86 CPM, so this week's gain is coming from lead volume, not click quality.

The Advantage+TG split flagged in recent weeks has intensified rather than settled: the original ad set 'VP_Lead_inst-form_Advantage+TG_01-04-2026' fell to ₹1,195 (from ₹6,739) while its 'Copy' now carries ₹6,056 of spend, up from ₹0 a week earlier. 'VP_Animated-Static_17July26' remains the account's clear anchor ad, spend up ₹2,657 to ₹6,974 with CTR improving to 0.88%, the same growth pattern confirmed for a third straight week.
actions: The Advantage+TG split has now run three weeks with spend consistently shifting into the Copy ad set. Consolidate into one ad set rather than continuing to fragment delivery and reporting.
'VP_Animated-Static_17July26' is still the confirmed anchor ad and climbing. Get a close variant into testing before frequency (1.21, up from 1.16) starts capping it.

CPL at ₹41.15 is holding at its best level in weeks. Keep budget concentrated on the anchor ad and the Advantage+TG split rather than the flat 'New House_25-02-2026' and 'Gruhpravesh' ad sets, which are still sitting at ₹0.

narrative: As of this run, the App Install CTWA ad set (previously blended into this tab) has been split into its own tab — the numbers below are Seemantonayan's true, unblended read for the first time. On that corrected basis, spend rose 32.3% to ₹7,986 (from ₹6,036), but chats actually fell 17.3% to 243 (from 294), pushing cost per chat up 60.1% to ₹32.86 and CPM up 41.6% to ₹35.91. That's a materially different picture than the last combined read (chats up 22.1%, cost per chat up 22.5%) — nearly all of that apparent volume growth was coming from the App Install ad set now reported separately; underlying Seemantonayan chat volume is actually declining while spend and cost climb.

'VP_Garbhsanskar_ 27July26' keeps absorbing more budget (₹1,587 to ₹2,525) while its CTR keeps softening (0.58% to 0.49%), the same decline flagged for three weeks running — with the App Install volume no longer masking it, this ad set's role in the tab's falling chat count is clearer. 'Testing_Broad_17Jun26' remains the single largest spend mover (+₹1,096 to ₹4,053), and CTR across the tab has dropped to 0.61%, its weakest reading yet.

callout.title: Numbers restated: App Install CTWA now split out
callout.body: As of today, the App Install/WhatsApp ad set ('VP_App-Download_31July26' — ₹1,042 spend, 116 chats this window) has moved to its own tab since it's a different objective. Everything above is Seemantonayan's corrected, unblended read; don't compare it directly against narrative from before this change without accounting for that.

actions: Corrected for the App Install split, chat volume is down 17.3% while spend is up 32.3% — that's a real efficiency problem, not the modest cost creep it looked like when the two were blended together. Treat this with more urgency than previously flagged.
'VP_Garbhsanskar_ 27July26' has had three weeks of declining CTR while absorbing more spend. Pause or hard-cap it this week rather than waiting further.
CPM up 41.6% week-over-week is a clear saturation signal in this audience. Expand into a new interest or lookalike audience rather than adding budget to the same broad testing ad set.
'Testing_Broad_17Jun26' is still the top spend mover in this tab — check its CTR on the next read before letting it keep growing unchecked.

narrative: New tab as of this run: this WhatsApp click-to-chat ad set drives app installs and was previously blended into Seemantonayan's numbers — it's now tracked separately since it's a different objective. Since launching around July 31, it's spent ₹1,042 across 8 days for 116 chats, a cost per chat of just ₹8.98 — dramatically cheaper than Seemantonayan's ₹32.86. CTR is a healthy 0.90% with hook rate at 26.45%.

Nearly all spend so far (₹1,008 of ₹1,042) has gone to the video creative 'VP_AppDownload_Video1', holding a 0.90% CTR; the static variant 'VP_AppDownload_Static-1' has only ₹34 of spend so far — too little to read yet. There's only one ad set running ('VP_App-Download_31July26'), so there's no spend-shift pattern to report yet; treat this as a single-ad-set, first-week baseline.

callout.title: New tab — early read, small sample
callout.body: Only 8 days and ₹1,042 of spend so far. Treat these numbers as a first baseline, not a stable trend — revisit after 2-3 more weeks of data before drawing conclusions.

actions: Cost per chat (₹8.98) is dramatically cheaper than Seemantonayan's (₹32.86) on early data. Worth a modest budget increase to see if that efficiency holds at scale.
Only one ad set and effectively one ad are running. Get a second creative variant into real rotation (the static ad has only ₹34 of spend) so there's a genuine comparison next read.
Too early to flag any spend-shift patterns — revisit ad-set/ad diagnostics once there's 2+ weeks of history.

narrative: The attribution-lag pattern flagged in earlier reads continues: Meta shows only 20 purchases against Shopify's 25 confirmed orders for the same window, holding 'Cost per Purchase (Meta)' at an artificially soft ₹317. Shopify's own numbers, unaffected by the lag, keep improving: orders up 150% to 25, revenue up 150% to ₹44,513, and ROAS climbing to 7.02x (from 6.62x on yesterday's read) — the best ROAS this tab has posted yet.

CTR continued to improve, up to 2.11% from 1.77% (+19.0%), and hook rate rose to 26.67% (+21.1%). Frequency has leveled off at 1.38, essentially unchanged from the 1.38 flagged last week as a rising watch item — no longer the near-term concern it looked like then.

'VP_Broad_AD+_31jul26' is now the dominant ad set (₹0 to ₹5,269) as 'VP_Broad_AD+_10Jun26' keeps tapering (down ₹5,236). At the ad level, 'VP_Umbartha_VideoAD_14-04-2026 – Copy' remains the anchor creative, spend up ₹1,573 to ₹5,613 with CTR ticking up again to 2.10%, confirmed for a third consecutive week.

callout.title: Same attribution lag, still resolving in Shopify's favor
callout.body: Meta's purchase count for this window's most recent days is still under-reporting (20 vs Shopify's 25 orders). Keep reading this tab off Shopify ROAS (7.02x) rather than Meta's 'Cost per Purchase,' which should self-correct in the next pull.

actions: ROAS at 7.02x is the highest read yet for this tab, with CTR and hook rate both still climbing. Push another modest budget increase — no saturation signs.

'VP_Umbartha_VideoAD_14-04-2026 – Copy' has now anchored spend for three straight weeks with improving CTR. Get 1-2 close variants into testing so a fresh option is ready once frequency (1.38) starts biting.
Frequency has flattened at 1.38 rather than continuing to climb — the concern flagged last week can be de-prioritized for now.
Expect Meta's purchase count for the newest days to keep reading soft. Don't react to it without cross-checking Shopify first.

narrative: Spend rose 11.5% to ₹12,173 (from ₹10,918) on 47 Meta purchases, up 27.0% — cost per purchase improved again to ₹259, down 12.2%, extending the efficiency gain flagged in the last two reads. Shopify confirms it: orders up 25.6% to 54, revenue up 22.9% to ₹42,338, and ROAS climbing to 3.48x, up from 3.36x yesterday — a third consecutive week of real ROAS improvement, not a one-off.

CTR held essentially flat at 1.34% (from 1.33%), matching yesterday's read and confirming the earlier softening has not resumed. Hook rate is still the one soft spot, down 5.3% to 13.81% — a smaller drop than yesterday's 7.5%, but not yet reversing.

'VP_Kundali-Namakaran_27Jul26' remains fully dominant (₹1,868 to ₹6,880). 'VP_Kundali-Namakaran_07-03-2026 – Copy' is back at ₹0 this week (from ₹4,247 the week before that), consistent with the retirement flagged in recent reads. 'VP_Kundali-Namkaran_VideoAD2_07-04-2026' is confirmed as the rising ad, now at ₹6,114 (from ₹0 the week before) holding a healthy 1.21% CTR, in line with the ~1.24% seen in yesterday's read, while 'VP_Kundali-Namkaran_VideoAD_26Jun26' remains parked at ₹162 of spend, roughly unchanged from yesterday's ₹168.
actions: 'VP_Kundali-Namkaran_VideoAD_26Jun26' has held near-zero spend (~₹162-168) for over a week now. The earlier call to retire it has held; no further action needed.
'VP_Kundali-Namkaran_VideoAD2_07-04-2026' keeps growing on a stable ~1.2% CTR with ROAS still climbing. Good candidate for a modest budget increase.
Hook rate is still soft (13.81%, down 5.3%) even as CTR and ROAS both improve — worth a fresh hook/opening-frame test on the top ad before it becomes a bigger drag.
ROAS has now improved for three straight reads (3.16x → 3.36x → 3.48x). Keep current budget allocation; no reason to pull back.
